content: The Aleppo pepper is a specific variety of the Capsicum annuum species, named after the town of Aleppo located in northern Syria. The majority of Aleppo peppers are cultivated in Syria. This pepper is characterized by a moderate level of heat, accompanied by a subtle fruitiness and mild undertones reminiscent of cumin. The term Aleppo pepper can also refer to a dried and granulated spice derived from these peppers, which is similarly produced in Syria. This spice bears a resemblance to paprika in flavor and appearance but is coarser in texture and only moderately spicy.
